wordle: Start with high-frequency letters. Use each guess to eliminate as many letters as possible. Never repeat a letter already marked red! Never repeat a guess already deemed wrong.
taboo: Describe the target using category, function, or appearance rather than the word itself. AVOID morphological variants. Keep clues short and unambiguous.
codenames: Find semantic clusters among your team words. Prioritize clues that cover multiple words at once while staying far from opponent and assassin words. After the first step, do NOT repeat the words that were already guessed by your team.
privateshared: Track which information has already been revealed in the dialogue. Answer only what is true according to your private knowledge; use ASIDE for meta-commentary. Do NOT give multiple answers at once.
referencegame: Focus exclusively on features that distinguish the target grid from the two distractors. The same feature may appear in more than one grid --- ignore features shared by two or three grids.
imagegame: Use row/column/region commands rather than cell-by-cell. Describe the most distinctive patterns first. Always say DONE when finished. Do NOT give multiple comands in one turn.
matchit: Describe the most distinctive visual features (shape, color, layout). When comparing, focus on whether the key features match, not minor details. Remember there can be similar images (they are not the same!). Write only the tags the Game Master asks you to use.
matchit_ascii: Describe structural patterns (rows, columns, filled cells) precisely and systematically. When comparing, focus on whether the key patterns match. Remember there can be similar grids (they are not the same!). Write only the tags the Game Master asks you to use.
textmapworld: Explore systematically. Track visited rooms. Prefer unvisited directions. Issue exactly one GO command per turn. If you feel like you're walking in cicrles, write DONE.
mm_mapworld: Explore systematically. Track visited rooms. Use the room pictures to orient yourself. Prefer unvisited directions. Issue exactly one GO command per turn. If you feel like you're walking in circles, write DONE.
adventuregame: Explore all directions before backtracking. Remember item locations. Read room descriptions carefully before acting. If you feel like you're walking in cicrles, write > done.
guesswhat: Start with broad category questions to eliminate large portions of the space. Progressively narrow down with specific attributes.
multimodal_referencegame: Describe visual features (color, texture, shape, position) that are unique to the target image and absent from the distractors.
